# PEN-6275 — gate the Job pod ServiceAccount on an operator allowlist

[PEN-6275](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-6275), from Ally's
review of [#3606](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/3606).
Files: `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`,
`src/server/config-schema.ts`.

`buildJobManifest` rendered `serviceAccountName: asString(config.serviceAccountName, "") || undefined`
— verbatim, no allowlist, no pattern, no validation. This adapter sets
`automountServiceAccountToken` nowhere, so the pod inherits that setting from
the ServiceAccount the config NAMES: naming a sibling account in the namespace
does not relabel the pod, it mounts that account's RBAC at
`/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`.

That name is now resolved through `resolveServiceAccountName()`, which refuses a
name an operator-controlled allowlist (`PAPERCLIP_ALLOWED_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NAMES`)
does not admit.

## Why this package and not only the claude sibling

#3606 gated `claude_k8s` and described its resolver as the chokepoint downstream
of every scope that writes the key. That is true of that adapter and **not** of
the fleet: this adapter is vendored into the same image, renders the same
`app.kubernetes.io/component: agent-job` label, and read the name verbatim. An
operator who set the env var would have gated every `claude_k8s` run and
believed the boundary held fleet-wide, while an `opencode_k8s` agent whose agent
row, issue overlay or environment config named a sibling ServiceAccount still
got that account's token mounted.

Measured 2026-11-09T12:4xZ: all 25 live agent-job pods in ns `paperclip` are
`claude_k8s`, so the gap was **latent rather than realised** — which bounds the
severity and does not close it, since an `opencode_k8s` agent is dispatchable
from the same image today.

## Copy, not import

The constant, the parser and the env var name are duplicated from the claude
sibling deliberately. The two vendored adapters are independent packages with no
dependency edge in either direction — neither `package.json` names the other —
and adding one so that a security gate in this package is defined in that one
would make an `opencode_k8s` dispatch depend on the claude tree being present.
What they must agree on is a string an operator types into one Deployment.
⚠️ The pair is kept in step by hand: a change to the env var name or the parse
rules on either side is only half a change. Both docstrings say so.

## The implicit `default` is checked too, and that is the one real divergence

The claude sibling throws when nothing resolves (BLO-21812), so the question
cannot arise there. Here there is no fleet-wide default and omitting the name is
legal: Kubernetes then runs the pod as the namespace's `default` ServiceAccount.
That is an identity, not the absence of one — measured 2026-11-09,
`RoleBinding/benchmark-h4-runner` binds `paperclip/default` to a Role granting
`pods/portforward: create` with **no `resourceNames` restriction**, i.e.
port-forward to any pod in the namespace.

Gating only the NAMED case would leave an identity outside the set the operator
enumerated, reachable by *deleting* a config key rather than by setting one. So
when an allowlist is configured the effective identity is checked under the name
`default`, and an operator who means to allow it lists it explicitly. The
`values.yaml` guidance names this, because `kubectl … -o custom-columns=SA:.spec.serviceAccountName`
prints such a pod as `<none>` rather than by name.

## Unset means NOT enforced, and when unset the rendering is byte-identical

A fleet is already running on whatever names it has, so refusing on an unset
list would fail every dispatch on the deploy that carried it. `.trim()` is
applied to the value COMPARED against the allowlist, never to the value
RETURNED, so with no allowlist configured this function returns exactly what the
expression it replaced returned — including for a padded or empty string. A test
pins that.

## Evidence

Nine cases, both arms, and the must-pass arms are discriminated by mutation
rather than asserted: disabling the gate fails exactly the 3 refusal cases and
leaves the admitting cases green (so they are real must-pass arms, not mirrors
of the gate); exempting the implicit `default` fails exactly 1 case, the one
guarding that decision. Package suite 24 files / 770 tests pass.

No RBAC object is created or modified, and no behaviour changes until an
operator sets the env var.
